title: Macroscopic scattering and the $q$-deformed double slit
html:
Remark. Macroscopic scattering and the q-deformed double slit

The substrate parameter q physicalizes wave propagation deformation. The slit material defines the brane boundary.

Wave propagation obeys the categorical Dirac equation (categorical Dirac operator):

\mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi =  0,

where \mathcal{D}_\nabla = q^{-1}\nabla + (1-q^{-1})\iota_\xi\nabla (variational equations). The test particle \psi is a photon with color content (color content). It propagates on an instanton background (categorical instanton).

The q-deformed differential is:

d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d.

As q \to 1, d_q \to d. For q > 1, the vertical differential introduces transverse momentum shift.

The Reeb contraction drives wavefront spreading (wavefront propagation). The phase difference along path \gamma grazing the slit boundary is

\Delta\phi =  \Delta\phi_{\mathrm{classical}} +  \hbar_q \int_{\gamma} \pi_V \circ d,

The integral depends on the slit material's torsion intensity. The Lagrangian simplifies on an instanton background (instanton on-shell):

\mathcal{L}_q\big|_{\text{instanton}} = c_2(A) + \psi^* \otimes \mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi.

An interactive simulation provides real-time parameter sweeps against the classical baseline.

Color content and polarisation-dependent interference

The color content modifies interference via:

1. Polarisation-weighted phase. Each polarisation mode acquires a Reeb phase. The total phase is

  \Phi_q^{(\mathrm{color})}(\gamma_j)
  = 
  \Phi_q^{(j)}
  + 
  \varphi_0q\Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(j)}
  + 
  \varphi_1(-q^{-1})\Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(j)}.

The bare-photon phase difference acquires a polarisation correction:

  \Delta\Phi_q^{(\mathrm{color})}
  = 
  \Delta\Phi_q
  + 
  (\varphi_0q - \varphi_1q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi.

2. Cross-color interference. Interference generates cross-color terms. This modulates fringe visibility:

  V_{\mathrm{color}}
  = 
  1 - |\varphi_0\psi_1 - \varphi_1\psi_0|^2.

Material-dependent decoherence stems from the Hecke algebra structure.

Observable signature. The correction is first order in \hbar_q for linearly polarised light. A double-slit experiment isolates this material-dependent shift.
